findings.source_passage: the whaleman is wrapped by influences all tending to make his fancy pregnant with many a mighty birth
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Alone, in such remotest waters'
findings.why_it_matters: This climactic sentence concludes Melville's extended meditation on why whalemen breed superstitions; it is rhetorically distinctive and interpretively important as a statement about imagination at sea. The entire passage ('Alone, in such remotest waters… chiseled hearth-stone') is collapsed without preserving this culminating image.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the closing sentence of the 'remotest waters' paragraph, including the image of the whaleman's fancy made 'pregnant with many a mighty birth.'

findings.source_passage: not only all his bodily woes, but all his intellectual and spiritual exasperations. The White Whale swam before him as the monomaniac incarnation of all those malicious agencies which some deep men feel eating in them, till they are left living on with half a heart and half a lung.
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'half a heart and half a lung' is one of the most distinctive and critically cited images in the chapter; the draft drops it, weakening the visceral intensity of the key characterisation of Ahab's consumed being.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'some deep men feel eating in them, till they are left living on with half a heart and half a lung' verbatim after 'malicious agencies.'

findings.source_passage: That before living agent, now became the living instrument. If such a furious trope may stand, his special lunacy stormed his general sanity, and carried it, and turned all its concentred cannon upon its own mad mark
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'It is not probable that this monomania'
findings.why_it_matters: The metafictional self-awareness ('If such a furious trope may stand') is a signature register move of Melville's narrator; the draft drops this clause while retaining the surrounding metaphor, erasing the self-conscious rhetorical irony.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'If such a furious trope may stand' to preserve the narrator's voice-establishing self-commentary within the cannon metaphor.

findings.source_passage: the subterranean miner that works in us all, how can one tell whither leads his shaft by the ever shifting, muffled sound of his pick?
findings.why_it_matters: The draft renders this as 'who can tell whither his shaft leads,' dropping 'how can one tell' and slightly reordering; a minor flattening of a rhetorical question that borders on set-piece prose.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the phrasing 'how can one tell whither leads his shaft' verbatim.

findings.source_passage: for one, I gave myself up to the abandonment of the time and the place
findings.why_it_matters: The draft substitutes 'the time and tide' for 'the time and the place,' introducing a cliché ('time and tide') that subtly degrades the original phrasing.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'the time and the place' exactly as written.

summary: The draft is broadly faithful and preserves the chapter's major passages verbatim or near-verbatim, but loses the 'half a heart and half a lung' image, the 'fancy pregnant' culmination, and the self-aware 'furious trope' clause—three medium-severity voice-flattenings that together thin Melville's most distinctive rhetorical register without reaching the threshold for regeneration.
